description: DNA is an Australian monthly for gay men that mixes news features, celebrity interviews and long reads on LGBTQIA+ life with extensive model and fashion photography. Every issue carries a cover interview, a themed feature and several photographic portfolios. It is for readers who want a glossy, international gay lifestyle title with an Australian base.

Doesn't Exist is a hardcover London magazine that looks at fashion through cinema. Each issue is built around a filmmaker or film movement, most recently an unofficial tribute to Federico Fellini, and fills it with fashion editorials, illustration, interviews and essays that answer those films. It is for readers who collect fashion photography and arthouse film culture in equal measure.

Dossier is a New York print magazine about travel, culture and style, relaunched in 2024 after an earlier life as a fashion and art title. Each biannual issue is organised around places, from the Mekong countries to Madagascar and Palm Springs, and mixes long travel features, fashion stories shot on location, photography, short fiction and conversations with chefs, musicians and writers. It is for readers who want slow, luxury leaning travel journalism with a literary bent.

72 is a quarterly London magazine of fashion, beauty and culture that launched in 2025. Each issue is themed and leads with cover stories shot by established fashion photographers, backed by long interviews, essays and portfolios on music, film, art and Black British culture, across several covers sold at random. It is for readers of glossy fashion titles who want a large, collectable quarterly rather than a monthly.

Encens is a Paris fashion biannual that treats clothes as a matter of history and craft rather than seasonal trends. Issues combine new photography with archive led features on designers such as Armani, Montana and Comme des Garçons, interviews with stylists and collectors, and portfolios reaching back to the 1970s and 1980s. It is for readers who collect fashion magazines as objects and care about design lineage.

Exhibition is an oversized Paris fashion and art magazine published twice a year, each issue built on a single theme and sold with four or more alternative covers by different photographers. Inside are fashion series by international photographers and stylists, conversations with designers and architects, and art portfolios at 33 by 44 cm. It is for readers and collectors of large, image led fashion publications.

EXIT is a British biannual of art, fashion and photography, around 196 glossy pages now sold as a hardback with a different cover star on each copy. Each issue mixes long fashion editorials and interviews with reproductions of work by artists and photographers such as Arthur Jafa and Irving Penn. It is for readers who collect image led fashion magazines with multiple covers.

Eye is the London review of graphic design and visual culture, published since 1990, with long profiles of designers and typographers, design history essays, critical columns and extensive reviews of books, type and exhibitions. It has been independently owned since 2008. It is read by working designers, educators and students who want criticism and history rather than portfolios.

FAR–NEAR is an annual book format publication from New York that looks at Asia and its diasporas through photography, essays, poetry and interviews, with contributors from Japan, Iran, Palestine, Vietnam and many countries between. Each 320 page volume is themed, most recently Heat, and is produced as a designed object with inserts and a fold out poster. It suits readers of art and photography books interested in Asian and diasporic perspectives.

FatBoy Zine is a London print zine about Asian food and identity, with each issue taking a theme or place, from Filipino food and Hong Kong to the diaspora and multi heritage cooking. Issues combine interviews with chefs and artists, commissioned writing and illustration, and a set of recipes. It is for readers interested in food culture, migration and design led small publishing.

filling Station is a Calgary experimental literary magazine publishing new Canadian and international poetry, fiction, literary journalism and visual art, with an emphasis on emerging and formally adventurous writers. Issues are loosely themed and present around twenty five to thirty contributors each. It is for readers and writers of innovative small press literature.

Flagrant is an American print magazine about basketball culture rather than match coverage, following artists, fans, community projects, fashion and the people around the game with heavily art directed photography and illustration. Issues are themed, from community to sustainability to a WNBA collaboration, and appear twice a year. It is for basketball fans who care as much about the aesthetics and communities around the sport as the scores.

Folding Rock is a Welsh print magazine of new creative prose, with short fiction, creative non fiction and literary criticism from Wales and beyond alongside art and photography. Each issue is themed and mixes established names with first time writers, and the latest, Treigl, is bilingual in English and Welsh. It is for readers of literary magazines who want contemporary writing with a Welsh centre of gravity.

FRAME is an English language interior design and architecture magazine from Amsterdam, in print since 1997, that concentrates on commercial and public interiors such as retail, hospitality, workplaces and exhibitions. Each issue is built around a theme, recently Speed versus Slowness, and mixes project features, interviews with practitioners and trend analysis about how spatial design is changing. It is for practising interior designers, architects, brand teams and students who want a professional view rather than home decoration.

FreeFall is a Calgary literary magazine publishing poetry, short fiction, memoir, essays, translations and author interviews twice a year, alongside the results of its annual prose and poetry contest. Each issue runs several dozen contributors, mostly Canadian, behind a commissioned cover artwork. It is for readers and writers of Canadian literary fiction and poetry.

Fucking Young! is a Barcelona menswear and youth culture magazine that builds each issue around one theme, recently Dopamine, Dreamcore and Transparency. It runs long photographic fashion stories with young models and musicians plus interviews with designers across roughly 400 pages and several collectable covers. It is for readers who follow menswear, emerging photographers and pop culture.

Full Pour is a quarterly American magazine about drinks of every kind, with sections on wine, beer, spirits, cannabis infused drinks and zero proof, plus coffee and tea. Each hundred page issue mixes reported features on producers and farming with short interviews and skips scores and buying guides altogether. It is for curious drinkers and trade readers who want cross category reading rather than a single beverage title.

GAYLETTER is a New York queer culture magazine that grew out of a weekly events newsletter. Each issue pairs cover stories with artists and performers, shot by photographers such as Collier Schorr, with interviews, nightlife, art and fashion photography, usually in two cover editions. It is for readers interested in contemporary gay and queer culture and the New York scene.

Girls Like Us is a Brussels queer feminist magazine devoted to women and trans people working in art, culture and activism, with each issue built around a theme such as economy, biography or the club scene. Issues combine essays, personal writing, conversations and artists' visual contributions, and the latest was made together with a closing lesbian and trans bar. It is for readers of feminist and queer theory, art writing and small press culture.

Glory is a football magazine that treats each issue as a travel document about one country, city or club away from the big leagues, with recent editions on San Marino, Hamburg, Hibernian and Mexico ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Issues run to around 240 pages of film photography from stadiums and streets, long essays, interviews and practical notes for visiting. It is for readers who love football for its fan culture and places, and for travel readers who use the game as a way in.
